differences.what: Lighting is a flat, cool blue ambient wash with no warm sources. The reference is dominated by warm amber-orange light: glowing heater columns, under-rail LED strips, lit planters, candles and paper lanterns, all against near-black shadows.
differences.where: Whole frame, worst on the terrace deck, railings and table area in the center
differences.fix: Cut blue ambient/fill by about 70% and darken the shadows to near-black. Make the heater columns, planter uplights, rail-base LED strips, table candles and lanterns emissive warm point/area lights (around 2200-2700K) so the deck and fences are lit warm from inside the terrace. Add bloom and tonemapping so these sources glow.

differences.what: Glass-and-timber pergola roof is missing. The reference has a dark timber beam grid holding a rain-streaked transparent roof over the whole terrace, with string lights hung under it, plus thick dark timber posts down both sides.
differences.where: Top third of frame and both sides (posts on left and right)
differences.fix: Build a pergola: thick dark-brown timber posts every ~2m on both sides, longitudinal and cross beams overhead, and wet glass panels (transparent, reflective, with rain-drip streaks) spanning the top. Hang the string lights in zigzag swags from beam to beam under the glass, receding to the far end.

differences.what: Railings are plain flat grey-lavender panels. The reference has dark-stained vertical wood-slat fences topped by long planter boxes overflowing with ivy, hanging purple wisteria and white/pink flowers, and bamboo on the right.
differences.where: Left and right sides along the full length of the terrace
differences.fix: Swap the panels for dark walnut vertical-slat fences (~1.1m) with a wooden planter trough on top. Fill the troughs with dense trailing ivy, cascading purple wisteria racemes on the left foreground, small pink/white blooms, and tall bamboo clumps in the right foreground. Uplight the foliage warm from below.

differences.what: Patio heaters read as flat orange-and-beige untextured cylinders with no glow. In the reference they are polished copper pyramid heaters: a reflective copper dome cap, a glass tube with a bright orange glowing heating element and grille, and a copper pole and base.
differences.where: Right side, foreground heater (right edge) and mid heater (center-right)
differences.fix: Model a dome-shaped copper reflector cap, a cylindrical mesh/glass chamber with an emissive orange core (strong bloom), and a polished copper pole. Use metallic copper PBR (metallic 1, roughness ~0.25) so it reflects the lights. Each heater should cast warm light onto the nearby deck and plants.

differences.what: Floor has no wet reflections. The reference deck is dark wood planking with a mirror-like puddle sheen that reflects heaters, stools and lights in long warm streaks. The capture floor is a matte navy plane.
differences.where: Bottom center deck, foreground to the vanishing point
differences.fix: Use dark wood plank flooring with planks running lengthwise. Set low roughness (~0.05-0.15) with puddle masks and screen-space/planar reflections so warm light sources leave vertical reflection streaks. Add small droplet ripples.

differences.what: Paper lanterns and signage are missing: the white chochin lanterns with the water-drop (雫) emblem, the pink neon '雫テラス' sign, the '関係者以外立入禁止' plaque, the red 'やきとり' sign, and the stone lantern.
differences.where: Lanterns on the left posts (upper left to center); neon top right; plaque on the right fence; red sign at left edge; stone lantern bottom right
differences.fix: Hang three or four white emissive paper lanterns with the drop-and-waves logo from the left posts, decreasing in size with depth. Put a magenta neon '雫テラス 💧' sign on the top-right building. Mount a dark metal plaque reading '関係者以外 立入禁止' on the right fence. Add a red lit 'やきとり' sign at the far left and a small glowing stone/metal lantern on the right step in the foreground.

differences.what: Tables and stools are low-poly flat orange shapes. The reference has round wet cream/brass-topped bistro tables on black pedestal bases, and tufted oxblood leather stool seats with chrome rims and legs. It also shows more tables receding (at least 3) with table-top props.
differences.where: Center: the table row and the stools on each side
differences.fix: Make the table tops smooth (32+ segments), glossy cream marble/brass with water beads, on black cast-iron bases. Give the stools glossy deep-red tufted leather with chrome rings and footrests. Add 3-4 table sets receding down the aisle. Put a candle holder, steaming teacup, small vase with pink flowers and a tent menu card on each table.

differences.what: Background buildings are dark-navy blockouts with black window holes. The reference shows detailed grey concrete apartment blocks with warm-lit windows, balconies with railings, AC units, and cyan neon edge strips.
differences.where: Background left, center and right behind the terrace
differences.fix: Fill in apartment facades: balcony railings, warm amber interior light behind curtains in about 40% of the windows, AC units and pipes, wet concrete with streaks. Run cyan neon strip lines along the roof edges on the left and right buildings. Add street lamps with a cool glow.

differences.what: Rain is rendered as big, bright white streaks crossing the whole view, including inside the covered terrace. The reference rain is fine and mostly seen as drips running off the roof edges and streaks on the glass; the area under the roof is dry-air.
differences.where: The whole frame, especially the center foreground over the tables
differences.fix: Stop rain from falling under the pergola roof with an occlusion volume. Make the outside streaks thinner, shorter and lower-opacity, lit by nearby lights. Add drip curtains along the roof eaves and running droplets on the glass panels.

differences.what: String lights are a single sparse swag of flat, unlit pastel spheres with no glow. The reference has many dense strands of warm-white bulbs mixed with red, pink, teal and green bulbs, each with bloom and reflected on the glass roof.
differences.where: Top of frame, running down the terrace to the vanishing point
differences.fix: Use 6-8 swags of small (~5cm) emissive bulbs on dark cable, mostly warm white (2700K) with scattered red, magenta, teal and green. Add strong bloom and let them reflect in the glass roof and the wet floor. Taper bulb size with distance to sell depth.
